issues.description: The problem statement's illustrative toString() example (problem_statement.md lines 36-39) shows numeric lecture attributes quoted as strings (e.g., numberOfInscribedStudents='600'), but the UML in the same problem statement (problem_statement.md lines 63-68) and the reference implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java lines 6-10) declare those attributes as int (lectureName is String, the student/lecturer/tutor counts are int). This mismatch in the example wording/formatting can lead students to wonder whether those fields should be declared as String or int.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the problem statement example consistent with the UML and reference code: remove the single quotes around numeric fields in the toString() example so they appear as numbers (e.g., numberOfInscribedStudents=600), or add an explicit note that the quotes in the example are only part of a printed representation and that the attributes should be declared as int. Update the example line in problem_statement.md accordingly.
